chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Hamza, from Ibrahim ibn Hilal, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A vessel containing both gold and silver, should I buy it with gold or with silver?' He said: 'If you are able to separate (purify) it, then do not (buy it); and if you are not able to separate it, then there is no harm (in buying it).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a mixed gold and silver vessel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled on the purchase of a mixed vessel containing both gold and silver, establishing that the permissibility hinges on the buyer's ability to effectuate separation (takhlis). If separation is feasible, the transaction is discouraged to avoid uncertainty (gharar) inherent in mixed commodities; however, if separation is impractical, the purchase is deemed permissible, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of easing hardship when the defect is unavoidable.
